title: The Grand Terrace in Chicago, 1936
summary: Jones recalls Basie fired at rehearsal at the Grand Terrace and kept on when Alma Turner defended them, playing for a month.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yes, because we had a big stinkeroo in '39. We was at the Paramount Theatre. But going back to this particular year, 1936, which was right after July - all at once we figured out a way to get Basie moving into East and booked him into the Grand Terrace, because Bennie Moten was supposed to go in the Grand Terrace and Bennie died. When Basie took over the band they said we'll bring Bennie in to follow Fletcher Henderson and Earl Hines, into the Grand Terrace, which we opened and closed the same night, at rehearsal. Elmer Turner was a dancer. Alma Turner was the soubrette.
You know the soubrette, the one that did the middle number.
That's a dance also, isn't it?

Oh, sure, a specialty, yes. But Alma had a specialty. She had an act; she came out with a chair, selling furniture. "Anybody want to buy my chair?" She was a very Creole type, out of Buffalo, but she did not say yes or no to Al Capone or nobody. They fired us at rehearsal because they bought bassoon parts and everything for Basie's band to play for the show, following Earl Hines and Fletcher Henderson. And, no! But prior to that I had walked into the Grand Terrace with Mr. Basie, with no band, no job, no money when Fletcher Henderson was playing there. Chu Berry was on the end and I was sitting ringside with Claude Williams, with (Maceo) Birch and Sam Baker, the guy that had kicked us out of the place in 1934, but this is 1936.
You only played one night at the Grand Terrace? You didn't even play one night?

Wait a minute, we were rehearsing and the man said, "You're through." And Alma Turner says, "What's wrong with you? What do you expect of these people? Why don't you go around and get the Chicago Symphony to play this music?" Alma Turner kept us at the Gram Terrace.
Oh then you did play there?
Yes, we were there for a month.
